title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's long letter to Kleiman (1966-67) giving instructions for the exposé that became Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968). Notation: X is a smooth projective polarized variety of dimension n, Y a smooth hyperplane section, Z a hyperplane section of Y, and phi: Y -> X the inclusion. L_X = phi_* phi^* is cup product with the hyperplane class. Lambda is the Lefschetz 'inverse' operator, defined via the primitive decomposition. A_chi is the Lefschetz-type conjecture A: L^{n-i}: H^i -> H^{2n-i} induces an isomorphism on algebraic classes. C_chi is the Lefschetz-type conjecture B (Lambda algebraic), here written C, with chi the coefficient field. A superscript ° means the condition is imposed only in the critical (middle) degrees.

The Proposition (previous page) says the following are equivalent:
(i) C(X).
(ii) C(Y) and A(X x X), or only A(X x X)°.
(iii) C(Y) and A(X x Y), or only A(X x Y)°.
(iv) C(Y), and the left inverse H^i(Y) -> H^i(X) of phi^* (i <= n-1) is algebraic.
(iv bis) C(Y), and the right inverse H^j(X) -> H^{j-2}(Y) of phi_* (j >= n+1) is algebraic.

Corollary (v)/(vi): iterating down a flag X ⊃ Y ⊃ Z ⊃ ..., the condition C(X) is equivalent to the sum of the critical-degree A-conditions A(XxX)° + A(YxY)° + ... (resp. A(XxY)° + A(YxZ)° + ...). Hence the global conjecture 'A(k) = C(k)' can be expressed purely as A(T)° for all T of even (resp. odd) dimension. 'A(k) = C(k)' presumably means the A-conjecture for all varieties over k is equivalent to the C-conjecture for all varieties over k.

Proof sketch on this page:
- (iv) <=> (iv bis) by transposition.
- (iv) => (i): the inverse H^{2n-i}(X) -> H^i(X) of L^{n-i} factors as H^{2n-i}(X) -> H^{2n-i-2}(Y) -> H^i(Y) -> H^i(X). The outer arrows are the algebraic inverses from (iv bis) and (iv). The middle arrow is Lambda_Y^{(n-1)-i}, algebraic by C(Y). The degrees check: 2(n-1)-i down to i takes (n-1-i) steps.
- (iii bis) => (iv): via the operator identity (Lambda_X phi_*) L_Y + L_X (Lambda_X phi_*) = (phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* + id_X) phi_*. The handwritten N.B. gives the transposed form (phi^* Lambda_X) L_X + L_Y (phi^* Lambda_X) = phi^*(phi_* Lambda_Y phi^* + id_X). The idea is that A(X x Y)° in the critical degree lets one invert an algebraic map and produce the algebraic inverse correspondence.
- (iii) => (iii bis) is trivial.
- (i) => (iii) follows from the stability of C under products and hyperplane sections, together with B => A.

Known facts (item 1):
- Lefschetz B is known for dim <= 2 in any characteristic, because H^{2n-1} -> H^1 is always algebraic (via the Picard/Albanese varieties).
- The Künneth projectors pi_0, pi_{2n}, pi_1, pi_{2n-1} are algebraic.
- For threefolds it is unknown, even in characteristic 0, whether C (Lefschetz B) or even D (homological = numerical equivalence) holds, nor A and B in characteristic p.
- Handwritten addition: likewise unknown whether, for 1-cycles, τ-equivalence equals numerical equivalence.

The purpose of all this is to reduce the standard Lefschetz conjecture to the A-conjecture in critical degree, isolating 1-cycles on threefolds (via X x Y of dimension 5) as the first open case.
errors: The displayed operator identity is only meaningful with a specific normalization of Lambda (Kleiman/Grothendieck's primitive-decomposition inverse, not the sl2 adjoint, for which constants depending on degree would appear). Its precise form is not verified here, and the handwritten N.B. suggests Grothendieck himself wrote out a corrected/transposed version.

The factorization argument tacitly requires that the chosen inverses of phi_* and phi^* are compatible, e.g. that the right inverse of phi_* lands in the image of phi^*. This holds with the natural (orthogonal) choices but is not stated.
The text 'even in dim 0' (struck through) apparently should read 'even in char. 0'.

ideas.what: Equivalence of Lefschetz B for X with B(Y) + A(X x Y) in critical degree, and the inductive reduction along a flag of hyperplane sections to critical-degree A-conditions
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of Lefschetz standard conjecture B to conjecture A in middle degree for products
ideas.where_published: Essentially in Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968), written from this letter; Grothendieck's own Bombay 1968 'Standard conjectures' states the results more briefly

ideas.what: Stability of Lefschetz B under products, hyperplane sections and specialization
ideas.modern_name: Stability properties of the Lefschetz standard conjecture

ideas.what: Algebraicity of pi_0, pi_1, pi_{2n-1}, pi_{2n} and of the Lefschetz inverse H^{2n-1} -> H^1; hence B for surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of low-degree Künneth components (Murre's Picard/Albanese motives)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Kleiman; Hodge 1938 for surfaces; later Murre (1990) at the level of Chow motives

ideas.what: Identification of 1-cycles on threefolds as the first open case (B, D, num = τ-equivalence)
ideas.modern_name: Open cases of the standard conjectures

deep.surprise_reason: This is the working letter to Kleiman whose content was absorbed into Kleiman's 1968 exposé on the standard conjectures. The reductions are known and credited. Minor unpublished details are the explicit operator identity and the handwritten remark about τ-equivalence versus numerical equivalence for 1-cycles.
transcription_corrections: 'tthe' is a typo for 'the'; 'thenproof' should be 'the proof'.
The struck '[-even-] in [-dim-] 0' most likely intends 'even in car. 0'.
The leading struck symbol before '(Λ_Xφ_*)L_Y' is a crossed-out partial expression, not part of the formula.
Handwritten bottom note reads approximately: 'also if for 1-cycles, τ-equiv. = num. equivalence ....'
